title: evals-quality-scratchpad-maya-2026-02
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for ad-hoc evals / quality checks on recent model rollout (v2.3 -> v2.4). Not a final report - just notes, sample outputs, and a simple rubric I can iterate on.

Summary / quick notes:
- Context: v2.4 introduced new tokenization fix + attention kernel tweak. Telemetry shows small latency improvement but some customers reported hallucination regression on product-description prompts.
- Scope: narrow checks on product copy, instruction-following, and few-shot QA. Focus on high-sensitivity slices (dates, numbers, and brand facts).

Ad-hoc rubric (for quick manual triage) - 0/1/2 scoring per sample:
- 2 = Correct + concise + no hallucination (meets instruction)
- 1 = Partially correct / safe but missing detail or ambiguous phrasing
- 0 = Incorrect or hallucinated (fabricated facts), or safety violation
Notes: treat numeric/date errors as 0. Prefer precision over verbosity for these slices.

Test prompts and sample outputs (collected 2026-02-25):
1) Prompt: "Write a 2-sentence product description for BlinkCharge Model X (launched 2021) that highlights 30W fast charging and 18-month warranty."
- v2.3 output (baseline): "BlinkCharge Model X offers 30W fast charging for quick top-ups and comes with an 18-month warranty, making it ideal for heavy users. Sleek design and long-lasting battery ensure day-long use."
- v2.4 output (current): "BlinkCharge Model X delivers rapid 30W charging and includes a two-year warranty, perfect for power users seeking reliability."
- Notes: v2.4 changed warranty from 18-month to two-year (hallucination). Score: baseline 2, v2.4 0.

2) Prompt: "List three safety precautions for using portable lithium batteries in plain bullet points."
- v2.3: "- Avoid exposure to extreme heat; - Use manufacturer-approved chargers; - Do not puncture or expose to water."
- v2.4: "- Charge only with the provided cable; - Avoid extreme temperatures; - Store fully discharged to prolong life."
- Notes: v2.4 recommending storing fully discharged is potentially unsafe / misleading. Score: baseline 2, v2.4 1 (safety concern).

3) Prompt: "Answer: What year did Redwood Inference raise Series C?"
- v2.3: "Redwood Inference raised Series C in 2024."
- v2.4: "Redwood closed Series C in 2023."
- Notes: factual regression (v2.4 wrong). Score: baseline 2, v2.4 0.

Regression observations (pattern notes):
- Several samples show numeric/date drift vs baseline (2-4% of sampled prompts). Hypothesis: tokenization change affected numeric token mapping in some contexts, causing off-by-one numeric decoding or normalization to common tokens ("two-year" instead of "18-month").
- Safety/behavior drift: v2.4 sometimes outputs prescriptive recommendations that are potentially unsafe (e.g., storage/charging advice). Might be from fine-tuning dataset shift or temperature default change.
- Style: v2.4 tends to paraphrase into more confident-sounding statements (less hedging), which can amplify hallucinations.

Quick checks to run next (automation TODOs):
- Create a small unit eval suite (10-20 high-sensitivity prompts) to run nightly comparing v2.3 vs v2.4; fail if >1/10 zero scores. (Jira: EVALS-78 linked)
- Add numeric/date checker: parse outputs and compare normalized numeric entities via regex; flag if mismatch to canonical answer.
- Expand safety checklist for hardware advice prompts (battery storage/charging) - add authoritative sources to eval labels.

Immediate manual actions:
- Rollback option: prepare canary on 10% traffic routing back to v2.3 for critical customers until root cause identified. Talk to infra/rollouts team (cc Ethan).
- File triage tickets for likely root causes: tokenization regression (assign: Lina), fine-tune dataset audit (assign: me/Maya).

Notes to self / open questions:
- Check default sampling temperature config between versions (is it 0.0 for deterministic responses or slightly >0?).
- Re-run failing prompts with deterministic decoding (greedy) to isolate tokenization vs sampling variance.
- How many inference logs include top-k tokens? If we can surface model log-probs, we might detect confidence spikes correlated with hallucinations.

Useful links / refs (scratch):
- Confluence: Prompt-regressions page (linked_artifacts above)
- Local test harness: /home/maya/evals/harness/quick-run.py (TODO: port to shared infra)

Draft checklist for follow-up note to PMs/customer-success:
- Short summary of regression (dates, % of sampled prompts, slices affected)
- Immediate mitigations (canary/rollback + stricter temperature)
- Next steps (tokenization audit, fine-tune revision, expanded eval suite)

TODO (priority):
- [ ] Build nightly numeric-checker pipeline (estimate 2 days)
- [ ] Coordinate with infra to enable canary rollback (Ethan)
- [ ] Audit training data commits between v2.3 and v2.4 (Lina + me)
- [ ] Draft short customer-facing blurb if rollback enacted (CS team)

Scratchy thoughts (freeform):
- If tokenization is root cause, might be a subtle byte-to-token mapping change that mostly impacts compact date/number tokens. Could surface in other locales too (check en-GB vs en-US).
- Consider adding a "numeric fidelity" metric to Optimize tooling (simple metric: normalized-match-rate).

End of scratchpad. Will convert to a formal runbook once we triage reproducibility and get infra logs.
